newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco, union reach deal to end Ontario strike.
newsitem.headline: Inco, union reach deal to end Ontario strike.

text.p: Inco Ltd. said on Thursday that negotiators for the 4,670 unionized workers at the company's Sudbury, Ontario nickel mine endorsed a contract deal to end a four-week strike.
Inco's Ontario division President Jim Ashcroft said the settlement package included improvements to wages, vacation bonuses, pensions and terms for contracting out work that striking miners sought.

"Our offer is fair and addresses the needs of both young employees and those nearing retirement," he said. "It is also vital to the division's competitive future and promises that the community of Sudbury will continue to benefit from a strong and competitive nickel industry."
The union said a ratification vote on the deal would be held on Saturday. Results of the vote will be announced late that afternoon.
The unionized Sudbury workers went on strike at midnight on June 2 after voting 60.4 percent against a previous contract offer endorsed by union leaders.
Union negotiators said the latest deal was struck after Inco, the Western world's largest nickel producer, agreed to concessions on wages, pensions and other issues.

"When the strike began, our members told us what the issues were: wages, pensions, vacations and contracting out. This settlement delivers on every one of those issues," said Wayne Fraser, chief negotiator for Local 6500 of the United Steelworkers of America.

According to Inco's 1997 production plan, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, 200 million pounds of copper and about four million pounds of cobalt this year.

Inco's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery, which processes cobalt, precious metals and electro-nickel, was unaffected by the Sudbury strike. Unionized workers at the refinery approved the contract on June 2.
Inco shares rose C25 cents to C$41.95 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday.
